warnings: Close() calls m.wg.Wait() THEN m.cancel(). For cooldown delays, runTurnAfterDelay must call wg.Done() when ctx.Done() fires. But Close() calls wg.Wait() before cancel() — this means pending cooldown delays will block Close forever unless something else cancels ctx. The task description's runTurnAfterDelay does 'case <-m.ctx.Done(): ... m.wg.Done()' but Close() does 'wg.Wait(); cancel()'. The coder MUST change Close() to call cancel() BEFORE wg.Wait(), or the TestCooldown_CloseDoesNotHang test will deadlock. New Close: m.cancel(); m.wg.Wait().
The running[name] flag must stay true during cooldown delay so concurrent triggers return Queued, not Started — don't delete it until the delayed turn actually starts or is cancelled.

When runTurnAfterDelay fires after delay, it calls runTurnAsync which calls defer m.wg.Done() — so runTurnAfterDelay must NOT call wg.Done() in the delay-expired path (runTurnAsync handles it). Only call wg.Done() in the ctx.Done() cancellation path.

TurnCooldown == 0 (zero value) means no cooldown — must preserve exact existing behavior. The cooldownDuration() helper returns defaultTurnCooldown when cfg.TurnCooldown == 0, but the caller checks cfg.TurnCooldown != 0 before using it, so zero-config skips the entire block.
drainQueue: when wasQueued and delay > 0, keep running[agent] = true (don't delete it) — it's implicitly true because we never deleted it. Only delete running[agent] in the !wasQueued branch.
The cooldown_test.go file must be in package watcher_test (external test package), not package watcher.
Iota ordering: Cooldown must come after Refused (value 4). Adding it before Refused would change Refused's value and break existing code.
